gaps.sentence: My brother is six foot three — he is much ___ than me.
gaps.explanation: 'Tall' is used for people's height, so the comparative is 'taller'; 'higher' is for heights above a level.

gaps.sentence: Pens, envelopes and paper are sold in the ___ department.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' is an adjective meaning not moving.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.
'Complement' means to combine well with or complete something; 'compliment' means to praise.
'You're' is short for 'you are'; 'your' shows possession.

gaps.sentence: A car remained ___ at the traffic lights for ages.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationary' means not moving; 'stationery' means pens, paper and other writing materials.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.
